title: Brent settles at $116.72, a four-year high, as Middle East flare-up lifts yields
content:
Brent crude rose 3.1% on 23 October to settle at **$116.72/bbl**, its highest since June 2022, as renewed violence in the Middle East, including Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, and fears of renewed US-Iran fighting threatened supply, according to AP and Bloomberg. The Dow fell 1.2% and the S&P 500 lost 0.5% to **7,623.68**, with nearly three in four constituents lower.

The 10-year UST yield edged up to about **4.99%** from 4.96%, so stocks and bonds fell together as energy-led inflation worries outweighed their usual hedging relationship. Futures price a Fed hold on 28 October, though some sources imply a hike is still possible. BofA's Michael Hartnett said he stays tactically risk-off until mid-November, while UBS argues robust earnings should support equities.

title: Meta's AI spending shock triggers tech selloff, with Nvidia and the Nasdaq under pressure
content:
Meta shares fell roughly 7–8% on 22 October, their largest drop since July, after the company raised its annual spending forecast to $135–145 billion and said it would fund AI investment through a new nonvoting share class. It also reported its first negative free cash flow as a public company, according to Reuters and other outlets. Sources differ slightly on the size of the fall.

The selloff spread: Nvidia dropped about **4%** and the Nasdaq Composite was on track for its largest decline in four months. Meta's five-year CDS widened to a record **119.3bp**, a sign that credit investors are questioning the cost of AI funding. The Nasdaq 100 finished broadly flat on 23 October, but the episode keeps AI financing in focus after the sector's earlier sharp losses.

title: Euro zone PMI falls to four-month low as France contracts and ECB meeting nears
content:
The HCOB euro zone flash composite PMI fell to **51.9** in October from 53.1 in September, below the roughly 52.7 consensus and its weakest in four months, Reuters and FXStreet reported. Services slipped to 51.7 and manufacturing to 52.4, while France returned to contraction amid rising energy-driven input costs. S&P Global said the reading is consistent with GDP growth of about 0.3% quarter on quarter.

French political turmoil also widened the OAT-Bund spread to a 15-year high, and the STOXX 600 closed down **0.31%** at 635.77, about 1.4% lower on the week, with Kering falling 16.6%. The data complicate the ECB's 29 October decision: it has hiked twice this year against oil-driven inflation, yet growth is now softening. The BoJ meets on 30 October and the BoE on 5 November.
